subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion + spillover ops (Q2)
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@orbital.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 renewal: dedicated pool + burst policy

Rafael,

Quick summary from our side ahead of the renewal: our production latency-sensitive endpoint needs more headroom. We're forecasting a sustained uplift for Q3 (batch + realtime mixed) and are evaluating: (a) adding 40 GPUs to the reserved pool, (b) a clear overflow policy for peak spikes, and (c) a throughput guarantee we can put in the SOW.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood commit to a 1.5M tokens/day throughput baseline with 99% availability for the reserved pool?
- During spikes, we're ok with spillover to on-demand but need bounds: max percentage of traffic spilled and priority behavior (real-time vs batch).
- Ops playbook: we need an on-call escalation and an SLO credit for sustained degradation.

Elena
VP of ML Ops
OrbitalAI

--

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@orbital.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 renewal: dedicated pool + burst policy

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the projection file. I looped Ben (sales engineering) and Laura (solutions/ops) since both will help lock the numbers and the runbook.

High-level answer: we can structure the renewal to add the reserved GPUs and include a measured overflow policy rather than a hard cap. Proposed outline (draft):

- Reserved capacity: add 40 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs in a new pool; customer can pin model versions.
- Throughput baseline: target 1.5M tokens/day as a commercial SLA; response-time SLOs scoped to route type (realtime vs batch).
- Burst/overflow: soft-spill to on-demand for up to 25% of minute-level concurrency during peaks. Beyond that, we apply graceful degradation (lower-cost quantized model fallback) and notify ops.
- Credits: pro-rated service credits if 15-minute rolling throughput falls below 80% of baseline for more than 3 consecutive windows in a 24h period.
- Ops playbook: 24/7 on-call, runbook with escalation to level-2 infra and model swap procedures.

I'm attaching a first-pass playbook PDF; Ben + Laura, can you review and add ops details and a cost delta? Elena, if this matches the run rate you'd expect, we'll convert to a formal amendment and include sample DocuSign link.

Best,
Rafael
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

--

Rafael / Laura — reviewed Elena's ask and your draft. A few operational items I recommend we capture explicitly in the playbook and in the SOW:

1) Capacity mix and hot-standby: reserve 60 GPUs for baseline (40 new + 20 rollover) and keep an additional pool as hot standby capacity that can be instant-spawned as on-demand; we should state boot time (target < 180s) and a 3-minute autoscaling cooldown to avoid oscillation.

2) Overflow gating: make spillover a per-minute percentage with a safety cap. Proposed: soft-spill to on-demand up to 30% of concurrent p99 concurrency. Beyond 30% we either (a) queue lower-priority jobs for up to 60s or (b) degrade to an optimized quantized model for realtime, depending on customer preference.

3) Throughput SLA and measurement: measure tokens/day at the model route level (UTC). SLA credit triggers: if sustained 24h throughput < 85% of baseline OR p95 latency for realtime > 350ms for more than 90 minutes cumulatively in a 7-day period, generate credits per the attachment formula.

4) Cost & credits: adding 40 GPUs + hot-standby increases committed monthly spend by ~ $65k; we should propose a tiered discount that scales with a 12-month commit. Also propose a one-time onboarding credit of 10% of the first month if Ops signs the runbook within 10 days.

5) On-call & escalation: include a named Redwood L2 rotation (Laura to own), primary Pager duty link in the runbook, and a 30-minute response SLA for Sev1 perf incidents.

I'll prepare an amendment clause with these numbers and send a redline to Rafael. Priyom, can you run the cost delta against the customer's projected mix (realtime 60% / batch 40%) and confirm the $65k number?

Ben
Sales Engineering

--

Elena — thanks for the review and patience. Per our internal review we've adjusted the commercial and ops terms so everything is explicit for procurement and SRE. Summary of the final proposal below (attached: proposed-amendment.pdf and ops-runbook.md):

- Commit: +40 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs added to your reserved pool (total committed = 60 GPUs). 12-month term; 5% tier discount applied to the reserved unit price.
- Throughput SLO: 1.5M tokens/day measured at the route level (UTC). Availability target = 99.2% monthly.
- Overflow behavior (final): soft-spill to on-demand up to 30% of p99 concurrency per minute. When spillover > 30% for more than 5 consecutive minutes, Redwood will (a) notify Orbital ops, (b) automatically route low-priority batch to a queued window up to 60s, and (c) optionally swap to a quantized model for realtime requests (customer toggle).
- Operational SLAs: 30-minute initial response for Sev1 perf incidents; 90-minute remediation target; on-call owned by Redwood L2 (Laura).
- Credits & exceptions: if 24h realized throughput < 85% of baseline for two consecutive days, the following credit applies: 5% monthly credit for each affected day (capped at 30% per month).
- Onboarding: 10% onboarding credit on the first invoice if the Ops runbook is signed within 10 business days.

Next steps:
1) Elena — please confirm acceptance of the terms so I can issue the DocuSign amendment.
2) Ben / Priyom — I'll need the final cost delta and the amended pricing line items for procurement (include the 12-month commit discount).
3) Laura — please finalize the on-call rota and paste the PagerDuty link in ops-runbook.md.

If OK, I'll send a DocuSign envelope and schedule a joint handoff call with your SREs next week.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
